category: Capital University of Science and Technology (CUST)
name: Accounting Principles
subject: accounting-principles

questions.question_text: Which accounting principle dictates that expenses should be recorded in the same period as the revenues they help generate?
questions.explanation: The matching principle requires that expenses be recognized in the same period as the related revenues to accurately measure profit.

questions.question_text: If a company purchases office supplies on credit, which of the following is the correct journal entry?
options: Debit Accounts Payable, Credit Office Supplies
Debit Office Supplies, Credit Accounts Payable
questions.explanation: Purchasing supplies on credit increases assets (Supplies) and increases liabilities (Accounts Payable).

questions.question_text: Which accounting principle requires that financial statements be prepared assuming the entity will continue to operate in the foreseeable future?
questions.explanation: The Going Concern Principle assumes a business will operate indefinitely, allowing assets to be recorded at cost rather than liquidation value.

questions.question_text: Which principle suggests that small items that do not significantly impact the decisions of financial statement users can be handled in the most convenient manner?
questions.explanation: Materiality allows accountants to ignore strictly rigorous accounting for insignificant amounts if it does not mislead stakeholders.

questions.question_text: Under the accrual basis of accounting, when should a company recognize revenue?
options: When the cash is received from the customer
When the performance obligation is satisfied
At the end of the fiscal year
questions.explanation: Revenue recognition under accrual accounting occurs when control of goods or services is transferred to the customer, regardless of cash timing.

questions.question_text: Which financial statement serves as a snapshot of the entity's financial position at a specific point in time?
questions.explanation: The Balance Sheet reports assets, liabilities, and equity at a single specific date.

questions.question_text: Which principle dictates that financial statements should reflect the economic substance of transactions rather than just their legal form?
questions.explanation: This principle ensures that the accounting treatment reflects the reality of the transaction, even if the legal structure suggests otherwise.

questions.question_text: When a company chooses to use the same depreciation method for all years, which principle is being followed?
questions.explanation: The consistency principle requires that once an accounting method is chosen, it should be followed consistently across periods to allow for comparability.

questions.question_text: Which principle implies that accountants should anticipate potential losses but not potential gains?
questions.explanation: The prudence principle dictates that when uncertainty exists, one should choose the option that does not overstate assets or income.

questions.question_text: The assumption that a business will exist long enough to fulfill its obligations is known as:
questions.explanation: The going concern assumption posits that the business will continue its operations indefinitely, justifying the valuation of assets at historical cost.

questions.question_text: Which principle requires that all information relevant to the user's understanding of the financial statements be included?
questions.explanation: Full disclosure ensures that financial reports provide all necessary info to prevent users from being misled.
